newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA sees slightly better year result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA sees slightly better year result.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Wednesday it expected a slightly better than expected result for the year to June 30, 1997.
CBA said the 11 percent rise in net profit to A$602 million for the six months to December 31, 1997 was due to better than expected growth in business volumes.

"Business volumes during the first half of 1996/97 were pleasing, leading to a better than expected interim result. This is likely to lead to a better than expected full year result," CBA managing director David Murray said in a statement.
Murray said the bank experienced strong growth in both lending volumes and deposits.
He said the cut in interest rates last year resulted in home lending growth above expectations.

"In addition, the bank's funds management arm, Commonwealth Financial Services (CFS), recorded strong growth in the sale of retail products, reaching A$2 billion for the six months, double the level recorded in the previous year," he said.
He said the first half result was also due to contined cost control and good credit management.

The first half result was above expectations of analysts, who had expected the bank to report a net profit before abnormals of between A$535 million and A$560 million, compared with A$541.9 million a year earlier.
CBA shares closed 17 cents lower at A$13.41 on Tuesday.
